summary: fix(sync): collapse the API's duplicate attachment entries before the upsert (issue #10)
reason: The Fiken API serves the same attachment twice inside the parent document: 78 of 85 synced sales on the test company carry a saleAttachments array holding two BYTE-IDENTICAL entries (same uuid, identifier, downloadUrl, filename, type). The mirror was ruled out as the cause — upsertGenericResourceTx replaces the data blob wholesale on conflict and a fresh re-sync left the array lengths unchanged — so the duplication is in the payload. Journal entries showed none on that company, but purchaseAttachments and the journal entry `attachments` array are the same shape from the same API and are cleaned too rather than waiting for the second report of the same bug. Nothing breaks today because the only reader, missing-bilag, tests for a non-empty array; anything that COUNTS or LISTS attachments shows every document twice. PLACEMENT: the clean-up is on every WRITE into the mirror, before the upsert, not at the read sites, because the two consumers that matter — the detectors and the MCP sql tool — both read the STORED blob rather than the response, so a read-side fix would have to be repeated in every future report and would be forgotten once. sync's upsertResourceBatch is not the only such write: writeThroughCache (both its list branch and its single-object detail branch) and writeMutationResponseToStore in internal/cli/data_source.go call store.UpsertBatch DIRECTLY, so with the dedupe only in the sync walker a `sales get` or `sales list` on the default auto data source rewrote the row sync had just cleaned with the duplicate pair back in it (review finding). There is no shared seam below those three: upsertResourceBatch lives in sync.go and adds discriminator grouping, and routing write-through through it would couple the read path to sync semantics for no gain, so the fix is one dedupeAttachmentArrays call wrapped around each of the four UpsertBatch arguments, each with its own PATCH comment. Four lines of generated code plus their PATCH comments; the helper and its tests are hand-authored in internal/cli/attachment_dedupe.go. KEY ORDER is uuid, then downloadUrl, then the CANONICAL BYTES of the whole entry, namespaced by the field the value came from so a downloadUrl that happens to equal another entry's uuid cannot collapse two documents. uuid is what the live payload identifies an attachment by but it is UNDOCUMENTED — spec.yaml's attachment schema (~4556) carries only identifier, downloadUrl, comment and type — so the chain has to survive its absence, and downloadUrl is the only DOCUMENTED per-file value. identifier is NOT A KEY at any position (review finding against the first cut of this patch, which had it second): spec.yaml:4559-4562 documents it as a USER-DEFINED label, "Could be the Invoice Id or receipt number for example", and no upload endpoint sets it per file, so an invoice PDF and its reminder on one sale — different filename, different downloadUrl, no uuid — routinely share it and keying on it DELETED one of two real documents. The last resort is the entry's canonical JSON (decoded and re-marshalled, so key order and whitespace do not matter): a byte-identical pair is exactly what issue #10 reports, and two entries equal field for field carry no evidence of being two documents, so this is the narrowest rule that still fixes the reported bug without identifier. An entry that is not JSON at all is kept as is — unreachable for an element of an array json.Unmarshal accepted, so a guard rather than a case — because dropping one would be real data loss to fix a cosmetic count. Order is preserved and the first occurrence wins, so the blob a reader sees is the API's own order minus the repeats. A document that loses nothing is not re-marshalled at all, so an unaffected blob stays byte-for-byte what the API sent, and the input slice is never mutated — the walker still holds the original payload after the call. The resource-to-field mapping is the EXISTING hand-authored attachmentsField table in missing_bilag.go (purchaseAttachments on purchaseResult, saleAttachments on saleResult, the bare attachments on journalEntry), reused rather than copied so the dedupe and the missing-bilag detector cannot drift on which field holds the array. A resource not in that table is returned untouched, including one that happens to carry a field by one of those names. Existing mirror rows are NOT migrated: they are cleaned by the next sync of the resource, which re-upserts the blob.
validated_outcome: make check green (go vet ./..., go test ./..., scripts/check-boundaries.sh) plus go test -race ./internal/cli/... ./internal/store/.... Hand-authored tests in internal/cli/attachment_dedupe_test.go: TestDedupeAttachmentArrays_CollapsesTheDuplicatePair drives the observed payload (two byte-identical entries) to one, checks the surviving entry keeps its fields, the rest of the document is untouched and the caller's slice still holds the original two; TestDedupeAttachmentArrays_KeepsDistinctAttachments asserts two real documents stay two AND that the unaffected blob is returned as the very same bytes; TestDedupeAttachmentArrays_KeepsDistinctFilesSharingAnIdentifier is the review finding — an invoice PDF and its reminder sharing one user-defined identifier stay two, with and without differing downloadUrls; TestDedupeAttachmentArrays_KeylessEntriesCollapseOnlyWhenIdentical asserts an identical keyless pair collapses on the bytes key while an entry differing in one field survives, in the original order; TestDedupeAttachmentArrays_KeyOrderDoesNotDefeatTheByteKey pins that the bytes key is canonical JSON, not raw bytes; TestDedupeAttachmentArrays_FallsBackThroughTheKeyChain covers downloadUrl when uuid is absent (including across differing identifiers), a shared identifier with differing downloadUrls staying two, uuid outranking a differing identifier and a differing downloadUrl, differing uuids staying two, and an empty key value falling through to the bytes in both directions; TestDedupeAttachmentArrays_AppliesToTheThreeCarriers pins the three field names and that contacts, invoices, credit_notes and transactions are returned untouched even when carrying a field by one of those names; TestUpsertResourceBatch_StoresTheDedupedBlob, TestWriteThroughCache_StoresTheDedupedBlob (list and single-object detail branches) and TestWriteMutationResponseToStore_StoresTheDedupedBlob read the row back out of a real store on a redirected HOME and assert the STORED blob holds one entry on all three write paths, which is the placement claim; TestWriteThroughCache_KeepsDistinctFilesSharingAnIdentifier guards the other direction on the write-through path. Every test except that last guard was checked RED against the pre-change tree: the identifier cases collapsed two real documents to one, and the two write-through tests stored the duplicate pair. No live API call was made and no fiken write command was run.
